title: Certificates of Deposit: Penalties Charged on Money Taken Out During a Grace Period
content:
The grace period that follows maturity on Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit exists so that the owner can take money out without penalty. Money withdrawn in grace therefore carries no penalty, whatever withdrawal kind its entry happens to have been recorded under. This page covers a penalty that was nonetheless charged on such a withdrawal.

## Standing of such a penalty

A penalty charged on money withdrawn during grace was charged against the certificate terms. It is credited back to the certificate with the adjustment reason of bank error. The credit rests on the certificate's own ledger and is owed without the owner having to ask for it.

The owner sees the credit as a new entry in the certificate's activity and as a higher principal balance from the moment it posts.

## Posting the credit with `reverse_grace_penalty_e6d62385`

The tool is kept hidden from the agent's tool list until it is unlocked. The agent unlocks it through `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and afterwards calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

### Capability

Each call posts a single penalty reversal entry on the certificate, dated the current day. The entry points to the penalty entry being credited back and carries the adjustment reason `bank_error`. The credited sum is added to the certificate's principal balance immediately; no other attribute of the certificate changes.

### Parameters

1. `certificate_id` — the reference number of the certificate on which the penalty sits, as returned by the certificate lookup for the customer.
2. `source_item_id` — the entry reference number of the penalty entry to be credited back, as returned by the certificate activity lookup.
3. `amount` — the sum credited back to principal, in USD to 2 decimal places, a positive figure rounded half-up to the cent.

The tool records the sum it receives and makes no judgement of its own about whether the credit is due.

### Receipt

A successful call answers with `reversal_id` (the new reversal entry's reference number), `certificate_id` (the certificate credited), `source_item_id` (the penalty entry credited back), `amount` (the USD credited, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD) and `principal_balance` (the new principal in USD, 2 decimal places). The presence of a `reversal_id` shows that the credit has posted.

## Basis Q&A

**The withdrawal entry was recorded as an early withdrawal although it happened in grace (hypothetical).** The label on the entry does not decide the matter; money taken out in grace carries no penalty.
